verdemorrow-seed-trials.title: Continuance trials
verdemorrow-seed-trials.text: Verdemorrow Agronomics says its Continuance seed lines have now come through forty growing cycles aboard working ships, from ore haulers to salvage tugs. Crews on long runs report fresh lettuce at the galley table and fewer arguments over the last tin of beans. The company is keen to add that a grow rack is not a farm: keep the air warm, the water clean and the nutrients coming, or the rack will let you know.
verdemorrow-seed-trials.mention: Verdemorrow reckon their seed has done forty cycles on working ships. Fresh lettuce every time, they say.

dwarf-wheat-shortage.title: Seed wheat short
dwarf-wheat-shortage.text: Dwarf wheat is in short supply along the inner routes this quarter. Brokers blame a poor season in the Tharsis greenhouses and a rush of ship crews who have discovered fresh bread. Verdemorrow Agronomics is asking spacers who grow their own to hold back some grain for the trials rather than eat the lot.
dwarf-wheat-shortage.notes: Also the bulletin that opens the arc verdemorrow-grain-sample.
dwarf-wheat-shortage.mention: Dwarf wheat is short all along the inner routes. Seems everyone has discovered bread at once.

galley-survey.title: Galley survey
galley-survey.text: A survey of long-haul crews puts a hot meal from their own galley ahead of shore leave, a working shower and, in one case, the captain. Hearth-2 owners were the most cheerful respondents, though researchers note they were also the only ones who had eaten that day.
galley-survey.mention: Some survey reckons crews rate a hot meal from their own galley above shore leave. Can't say I disagree.

firstlight-advert.title: Firstlight-4
firstlight-advert.text:
Verdemorrow Firstlight-4
Four trays, one crop, no excuses. Fresh greens on any ship with power, water and a crew who remembers to harvest. Verdemorrow Agronomics: where we go, life grows.

groundwork-advert.title: Groundwork
groundwork-advert.text:
Groundwork Nutrients
Your crop cannot live on ration bars, and frankly neither should you. Groundwork charges dose by hand or through a W2 water supply. Ask for them at the supply kiosk.

verdemorrow-grain-sample.title: A grain sample for Verdemorrow
verdemorrow-grain-sample.notes: A short pilot arc: grow and deliver one portion of dwarf wheat grain, paid in seed and nutrients (about 75 cr of goods for a 30 cr portion). It may start once the player has a Firstlight-4 rack installed.

message.text: Hello, [player-first]. We hear the [ship] runs a Firstlight-4. Our seed trials want grain grown out here on a working ship, not in a lab. Grow some dwarf wheat and bring us one portion of grain. We pay in seed.

objective.title: Grow dwarf wheat for Verdemorrow
objective.description: Plant Continuance seed wheat in a Firstlight-4, harvest it and carry one portion of wheat grain. Seed wheat is sold at station supply kiosks.

objective.title: Take the grain to a station
objective.description: Dock at any station while carrying one portion of wheat grain. Verdemorrow collects it from there.

message.text: Sample received, and it smells like bread. Three packets of seed wheat and some Groundwork nutrients, with our thanks. Keep the [ship] growing.

rack-hum.line: That grow rack hums all night. I can hear it through the bulkhead.

flatbread-joke.line: What's the difference between Hearth flatbread and a ration bar? Eighty-four hours of wheat and somebody who cares.

crop-worry.line: Every time the cabin warms up I think the crop's going to cook. Then I go and check the panel again.

kiosk-potatoes.line: Saw a hauler crew trading their own potatoes at the kiosk. Potatoes. Out here.

verdemorrow-beginnings.line: Old hand told me Verdemorrow started with one rack bolted into an ore hauler's galley. Probably true, the way they tell it.

unnamed-crop.line: Never name a crop before it's harvested. Everybody knows that.

verdemorrow-idea.text: Verdemorrow Agronomics was founded on a simple idea: a crew that grows some of its own food goes further between stations. Its line, Where we go, life grows, is printed on every seed packet it sells.

first-lettuce.text: Spacers on long hauls swear that the first fresh lettuce after a month of ration bars tastes better than anything a station galley serves.

trial-notes.notes: Given on a data card with the grain-sample reward (Agriculture 0.62.0); read on any computer or PDA.
trial-notes.name: TRIAL_NOTES.TXT
trial-notes.text:
VERDEMORROW AGRONOMICS - CONTINUANCE TRIALS
Shipboard sample log, dwarf wheat

Sample received in good order from the [ship]. Grain dry, clean, no mould. Germination test: strong.

Field note: crews keep asking whether wheat is worth the rack space. One portion of grain is not much. A flatbread on a cold shift is another matter.

Next trials: soybeans aboard ore haulers, and whether lettuce minds the noise of a refinery next door. Volunteers welcome. Send samples to any station.

verdemorrow-agronomics.label: Verdemorrow Agronomics
verdemorrow-agronomics.title: Verdemorrow Agronomics
verdemorrow-agronomics.body:
Verdemorrow Agronomics makes equipment for growing and cooking food aboard working ships. Its name is meant to suggest green growth and tomorrow, and its line, Where we go, life grows, is printed on every seed packet.

The company sells four lines. Firstlight cultivation racks grow a crop in four trays under their own lights. Hearth galley cookers turn produce into meals. Continuance is planting stock: seed potatoes and seed packets. Groundwork covers nutrients, water supply units and the benches that recover nutrients from crop waste.

Verdemorrow's pitch is modest by station standards. A rack will not feed a crew on its own, but fresh food, a little less to buy at each dock and something growing aboard make a long run easier.

growing-food-aboard.label: Growing food aboard
growing-food-aboard.title: Growing food aboard
growing-food-aboard.body:
A grow rack needs what a crew needs, only more steadily: power, water, warm air at a comfortable pressure, and a little carbon dioxide, which people breathe out anyway. Add nutrients, plant the seed and keep the cabin steady until harvest.

Most of what goes wrong is the room, not the plant. A cabin that gets too hot or too cold stops a crop growing, and one left that way long enough loses it. The rack's panel says what it is waiting for.

Nothing grown aboard is free. Every kilogram of food comes from water, nutrients, carbon from the air and the electricity that lights the trays, and what the crop does not use ends up as residue to deal with.
